subject: Targeted log redaction, escrow copies & regulator evidence — Veridian Health
messages:
From: Anika Rao <anika.rao@veridianhealth.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@veridianhealth.com
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Targeted log redaction + escrow for regulator review

Hi Lukas / Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our regulator has asked for two things specific to tenant-scoped audit logs for EU tenants: a) an ability to demonstrate that PII-containing lines can be redacted from in-place audit logs while preserving an auditable journal of what was redacted, and b) an escrow/verified snapshot option we can present as part of an inspection (with chain-of-custody metadata).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
- perform targeted in-place redaction for a single tenant (not global) and produce a redaction journal that timestamps each redaction,
- export a read-only snapshot (escrow) of the last 90 days of audit events for an identified tenant and store it in a customer-provided S3 in eu-west-1,
- provide an attestation template or SOC 2 mapping we can hand to the regulator showing controls around deletion/escrow?

Regulator expectation is we can produce both artifacts within two weeks of a formal request. We appreciate any constraints or suggested changes to that timeline.

Attached is our CAIQ excerpt they referenced. Let me know if you'd prefer a quick call; I can pull in our legal/compliance lead.

Thanks,
Anika Rao
Compliance Lead — Veridian Health
Anika.Rao@veridianhealth.com

(attachment: CAIQ_section_veridian.pdf)

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anika Rao <anika.rao@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Targeted log redaction + escrow for regulator review

Hi Anika — thanks for the clear ask and the CAIQ excerpt. Opening with short answers and then a proposed path: 

Short answers (high level):
- Targeted redaction: yes, we can redact tenant-scoped entries. We maintain a redaction journal that records the original event id (hashed), timestamp, operator id, and redaction reason.
- Escrow snapshot: yes — we can produce a read-only, timebound snapshot of audit events and deposit to a customer-controlled S3 bucket in eu-west-1. We can include a checksum manifest and signed metadata for chain-of-custody.
- SOC 2 / attestation: we can map the procedures to our SOC 2 control IDs and provide a standard attestation letter; for regulator-facing evidence we usually supplement with a tailored exhibit.

Constraints and notes:
- In-place redaction is irreversible for plaintext fields once redaction is executed; we keep a hashed pointer in the journal but do not retain raw PII unless escrowed.
- Escrow snapshot creation requires a reserved maintenance window (typically 1–3 hours for tenant-scale >100M events) if the dataset is large — this prevents index churn during export.

Next steps I recommend: 
1) Priya, can you confirm legal/compliance template language and whether a signed attestation is acceptable, or if Veridian needs notarization?
2) Marissa — can ops confirm an estimated time-to-provide for a 90-day escrow snapshot for a typical Veridian tenant size (we'll attach our retention matrix).

I attached a quick retention matrix for context. Happy to schedule a 30-minute sync if easier.

Best,
Lukas Meyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: RetentionMatrix_v1.xlsx)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anika Rao <anika.rao@veridianhealth.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Targeted log redaction + escrow for regulator review

Thanks Anika — looping in legal/compliance guidance.  Quick runbook proposal below that aligns with SOC 2 evidence needs: 

Proposed approach (for Veridian EU tenants):
1) Redaction workflow:
   - Operator opens a redaction request with tenant id and event ids (or time range).
   - System replaces PII fields with a standardized token <REDACTED:v1> and records a redaction journal entry: {event_hash, redaction_ts, operator_id (Redwood), redaction_reason, redaction_method}.
   - Journal is write-once; entries are retained for 7 years to support audits but do not contain the raw PII (only salted hashes).
2) Escrow snapshot:
   - Export tool generates newline-delimited JSON of audit events for requested window, produces manifest checksums, signs manifest with Redwood KMS, and uploads to a customer-provided S3 path in eu-west-1.
   - We provide both a machine-readable manifest and a human-readable attestation describing the export process and chain-of-custody.
3) Attestation and artifacts:
   - Provide SOC 2 control mapping (SOC2-Audit-IDs) and an attestation letter. If regulator requires, we can provide a notarized affidavit via our legal team (additional lead time).

Timelines (estimate):
- Sample redaction-journal template: 2 business days (we'll attach a template).
- Escrow snapshot for 90 days (typical Veridian tenant ~40M events): 7–10 business days including verification.
- Attestation/doc exhibit: 3 business days.

Privacy/legal note: if Veridian wants escrow stored under a contract that prohibits Redwood from rehydrating raw PII outside of export requests, we can add explicit contract language; that will be a contract addendum.

I will attach the redaction journal template and a draft escrow addendum (for internal review).  Marissa, please confirm any operational caveats.

Regards,
Priya Natarajan
Director, Privacy & Compliance — Redwood Inference
(attachment: redaction-journal-template.csv)

From: Anika Rao <anika.rao@veridianhealth.com>

Cc: security@veridianhealth.com
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Targeted log redaction + escrow for regulator review

Thanks Priya — this is helpful. Two quick clarifications from the regulator's checklist: 
1) They prefer in-place redaction where possible rather than re-hydrating raw PII from escrow for their inspection. Can you confirm the redaction tokenization approach preserves sufficient context for forensic analysis (i.e., we can still show event flows without revealing PII)?
2) For the write-once journal, the regulator insisted on an exportable CSV that includes the salted hashes and redaction reasons for each event. Is that what your template provides?

Also — could you share the sample redaction journal you mentioned (even with example hashed values) and a short SLA statement for irreversible deletions (we need to show the regulator that deletions are operationally enforced and auditable)? If needed we can set a 30-minute slot tomorrow for a quick walkthrough (we're in CET; I can do 16:00 CET).

Best,
Anika
